paragraphs.notes: Continuation page inside claim 1 (Patentansprueche begin on printed page 79 = p81, so this page is claims, not description). The whole body is one unbroken enumeration of substituent group names: it opens mid-word with lower-case "heteroarylaminosulfonyl," (the tail of "gegebenenfalls substituiertes N-Alkyl-N-" printed at the foot of p83) and closes with a comma after "Cycloalkylalkenyloxycarbonyl,", with no terminating punctuation. The patent carries no [00NN] paragraph markers, so marker is null. Transcription joins the 34 printed lines into flowing text; where a line ended with a word-internal hyphen ("Alkenylsulfonyl-N-Alkyl-" + "amino", "Heteroarylalkylsulfonyl-N-" + "alkyl-amino", "Heteroarylalkenylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-" + "amino") the halves are joined without a space. Nothing on this page is German prose; every token is a chemical group name, so en differs from zh only in lower-casing the names and in rendering German "Alkinyl" as English "alkynyl", following the convention already used in this run's other vision files. Printed as-is and not corrected: the sulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino series is inconsistently capitalised, "Alkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino" then five members with capital "N-Alkyl-" (Alkenyl-, Alkinyl-, Cycloalkyl-, Cycloalkylalkyl-, Cycloalkylalkenyl-) and then lower-case "N-alkyl-" again from Cycloalkylalkinylsulfonyl onward; and the entry between "Heteroarylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino" and "Heteroarylalkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino" is printed "Arylalkylsulfonyl-amino", without the "N-alkyl" the parallel members all carry. This claims copy of the list is word for word identical to the description copy already transcribed on p21 and p22, the same two anomalies included. A small stray ink mark sits above "Arylsulfonyloxy" on the fourth line; the same speckle appears at the same place on p80 and p81, so it is a recurring scan artifact, not a printed character.
